subject: Updating a global variable from within simmer

messages.author: 9631c5ae1a516d96
messages.subject: Updating a global variable from within simmer
parts:
First, let me begin by thanking the developers for the impressive work they have done. I can think of nothing that I used to do using commercial software that I cannot do using Simmer.


I am trying to reduce the number of attributes used in a simulation. There is a set of 6 attributes that may or may not be used before the simulated patient leaves the model. These attributes are patient-specific treatment effects; thus, they must be set as the patient enters the model. When simulating 100,000 patients and repeating this simulation 1,000 times while varying key parameters, then updating a set of 6 variables/cells in the global environment and reading from them when needed (I think) will be of great advantage.


I understand that I could just use global attributes. However, because these 6 attributes are called when a patient switches treatment, using global attributes the code will be rigid (hardcoded) compared to using a matrix/dataframe/tibble.


To give a simple example of what I want to achieve:

rm(list = ls())






library(simmer)




env = simmer()




global_var = 0




entry = trajectory() %>%

  set_attribute(keys = "test", values = function() rnorm(1)) %>%

  global_var = get_attribute(env, "test") * age^2




env %>%

  add_generator("tests", entry, function() 1, mon = 2)


Any help will be appreciated, thank you.

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Updating a global variable from within simmer
parts:
To write complex R structures in the global environment, you need to
use the <<- operator in any function. There are examples in these
scenarios:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-05-simpy.html#gas-station-refuelling
https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g#mobile-traffic-backhauling-with-fttx

Iñaki
